units.title: Tu vida de ahora
units.goal: Distinguir hábitos, situaciones temporales y estados; ampliar tus respuestas.

rules.title: Lo habitual y lo temporal
rules.text: Usa present simple para hábitos y hechos: I work. Usa am/is/are + verbo en -ing para acciones de ahora o situaciones temporales. Una situación temporal puede durar semanas; no tiene que estar ocurriendo en este segundo. Las expresiones usually y at the moment ayudan, pero decide según el significado.
rules.pattern: I usually work… / I am working…
examples: I usually study in the evening.
I am staying with my aunt this week.
She is working from home today.
rules.tip: No omitas be: I studying no es una oración completa.

rules.title: Frecuencia y preguntas
rules.text: Los adverbios de frecuencia suelen ir antes del verbo principal, pero después de be. Every day suele ir al final. Para preguntar por hábitos usa do/does; para acciones en curso invierte be y sujeto. How often pregunta la frecuencia. Una respuesta más útil añade un detalle: Twice a week, after school.
rules.pattern: How often do you…? / What are you doing?
examples: I hardly ever watch television.
My brother is always busy.
How often do you visit your cousins?
rules.tip: Hardly ever ya expresa una frecuencia casi nula: no añadas not.

rules.title: Estados y preferencias
rules.text: Know, understand, want, need, like y belong suelen expresar estados y normalmente se usan en simple, incluso ahora. Think significa tener una opinión en I think it is good; thinking about puede describir una actividad mental. Aprende primero los usos frecuentes y explica tus preferencias con because.
rules.pattern: I prefer… because…
examples: I prefer quiet places because I can read.
This bag belongs to my sister.
I do not understand this question.
rules.tip: I am knowing no es la forma habitual de decir lo sé.

questions.prompt: Usually I walk, but today I ___ the bus.
questions.why: Today presenta un cambio temporal: am taking.
La acción está en curso: is + studying.
Often suele ir después de be.

questions.prompt: ___ do you exercise? — Twice a week.

questions.why: Belong expresa pertenencia y lleva -s con this coat.

units.story: On most weekdays, Elena leaves home at eight and walks to college. She usually studies in the library after class. This month, however, the library is closed, so she is studying at her cousin Marco’s flat. Marco works in a café and is often busy in the afternoon. Today he is not working, and they are making lunch together. Elena prefers the library because it is quiet, but she likes spending time with Marco. They are planning to study together again on Friday. Elena does not want to change her routine forever; she only needs a place to study until the library opens.

reading.prompt: ¿Por qué estudia Elena en otra casa?
reading.why: El texto dice que la biblioteca está cerrada este mes.
This month y until indican una situación limitada.

dialogue: What do you usually do after class?
I usually study in the library.
Are you studying there this week?
No, I am studying at my cousin’s flat.
Why do you prefer the library?
Because it is quiet and close to college.
units.writing: Escribe 50–70 palabras: dos hábitos, un cambio temporal y la razón del cambio. Usa usually, this week y because.
units.model: I usually study at home and I often listen to music after dinner. This week, I am staying with my grandmother because my parents are away. I am studying in her kitchen. It is quieter than my house. I like being here, but I also want to see my friends at the weekend.

listening.text: Hi, it is Marco. I usually work on Fridays, but I am not working this Friday. The café is closed for repairs. I am meeting Elena at my flat at three. Please bring your English notebook. We can study first and then make a snack.

questions.answer: El café está cerrado por reparaciones.
options: El café está cerrado por reparaciones.
Está de vacaciones en otro país.

units.mission: Habla 45 segundos: cuenta cómo es tu semana normal y qué haces diferente esta semana. Pregunta a otra persona How often…? y responde con un detalle.

units.title: Personas y relaciones
units.goal: Describir personas, identificar de quién es algo y explicar relaciones.

rules.title: Aspecto y personalidad
rules.text: What does she look like? pregunta el aspecto físico. What is she like? suele preguntar personalidad o características. Usa be con adjetivos y have/has con rasgos: He is tall; he has curly hair. Hair suele ser incontable al describir el pelo de una persona. Añade and o but para conectar dos características.
rules.pattern: She is friendly. / She has curly hair.
examples: My neighbour has short curly hair.
My colleague is quiet but friendly.
What is your flatmate like?
rules.tip: No confundas What is she like? con What does she like?, que pregunta gustos.

rules.title: Mío, tuyo, suyo
rules.text: My, your, his, her, its, our y their acompañan a un nombre. Mine, yours, his, hers, ours y theirs lo sustituyen. Whose pregunta de quién es algo. Los posesivos no llevan apóstrofo: hers, no her’s. Con nombres propios, sí aparece el posesivo: Leo’s jacket.
rules.pattern: Whose bag is this? It is mine.
examples: This notebook is mine.
Their room is larger than ours.
Is that jacket yours?
rules.tip: El posesivo no cambia según el género del objeto: her car puede ser un coche de ella.

rules.title: Identificar con who y that
rules.text: Para identificar a una persona puedes añadir who + información; para una cosa, that o which. Estas frases se unen al nombre sin repetir he/she/it como sujeto. Aquí practicamos cláusulas que identifican: the person who lives next door. Puedes describir relaciones sin conocer un adjetivo exacto.
rules.pattern: The person who… / the thing that…
examples: She is the friend who helps me study.
This is the book that explains the rules.
I get on well with my new flatmate.
rules.tip: No digas the friend who she helps me: who ya es el sujeto.

questions.why: Look like se refiere al aspecto.
Los rasgos con hair se expresan con have.

questions.prompt: That is my coat. It is ___.
___ keys are these? — They are Ana’s.
Leo is the person ___ lives upstairs.
This is the phone ___ has a red case.
questions.why: That introduce información que identifica una cosa.

units.story: My new flatmate is called Sam. He is tall and has straight brown hair. At first, I thought he was shy because he did not talk much. Now I know that he is friendly and very patient. He is the person who helps me with difficult homework. We share a kitchen, but we have separate bedrooms. Mine is smaller than his, so I keep some books in the living room. Sam likes music and I like films. We do not enjoy all the same things, but we get on well because we listen to each other and share the housework.

options: Ahora cree que Sam es grosero.
reading.why: Al principio parecía tímido; después lo conoce mejor.
Mine sustituye a my bedroom.

dialogue: What is your new flatmate like?
He is friendly and very patient.
No, it is his. Mine is in my room.
Yes, we share the housework and help each other.
units.writing: Describe a una persona en 50–70 palabras: aspecto, personalidad, relación y una cosa que le pertenece. Usa who y un posesivo como mine o hers.
units.model: My cousin Rosa has short dark hair and brown eyes. She is friendly and very patient. She is the person who helps me practise English every weekend. We both enjoy music, but her guitar is better than mine. I like spending time with her because she listens carefully and always makes me laugh.

listening.text: We have found a blue jacket in the meeting room. It has a small notebook in its pocket. The notebook belongs to a person called Julia. If the jacket is yours, please collect it from Ben, the colleague who works at reception. Reception closes at six today.

units.mission: Describe a alguien durante un minuto sin decir su nombre. Otra persona debe identificarlo. Pregunta Whose…? usando tres objetos reales.

units.title: Historias del pasado
units.goal: Contar acontecimientos terminados con verbos regulares e irregulares.

rules.title: Afirmaciones en pasado
rules.text: Past simple sitúa una acción en un periodo terminado: yesterday, last year, two days ago. Los verbos regulares suelen añadir -ed; study cambia a studied y stop a stopped. Los irregulares tienen formas propias: go/went, see/saw, take/took. La forma de pasado es igual con todos los sujetos excepto be.
rules.pattern: Sujeto + pasado + momento terminado
examples: We visited the museum yesterday.
She went home after lunch.
They took the early bus.
rules.tip: Aprende irregulares en frases; no añadas -ed a went o saw.

rules.title: Preguntas y negaciones con did
rules.text: Usa did + sujeto + verbo base para preguntar y did not/didn’t + verbo base para negar. El pasado ya lo marca did: Did you go?, no Did you went? Be es distinto: Was she there? y She wasn’t there. Las preguntas con who como sujeto pueden ser Who called you?, sin did.
rules.pattern: Did you find it? / I did not find it.
examples: Did you enjoy the concert?
I did not lose my keys.
Who called you last night?
rules.tip: Distingue Who called you? de Who did you call?: cambia quién realiza la acción.

rules.title: Ordenar los hechos
rules.text: First, then, after that y finally organizan una narración. Before y after relacionan acciones o momentos. Ago se coloca después de la cantidad de tiempo: three days ago. Añade una reacción o resultado para que el relato no sea solo una lista de verbos. En un cuento terminado mantén el pasado.
rules.pattern: First… Then… Finally…
examples: First we bought the tickets.
Then we waited outside the station.
Finally we arrived at the hotel.
rules.tip: Last Monday no lleva in, on ni the en esta expresión.

questions.prompt: Last Saturday we ___ to the beach.

questions.why: Después de did va el verbo base.
Be forma la negación directamente: were not.
Ago va después de la cantidad.
Finally marca el final de una secuencia.

units.story: Last Saturday, Pablo went to a concert with his sister. First, they took a bus into town and bought sandwiches near the theatre. They arrived early, so they had time to walk around. At the door, Pablo could not find his ticket. He looked in his jacket and his bag, but it was not there. His sister asked, “Did you put it in your phone case?” Luckily, she was right. They found their seats just before the music started. After the concert, they missed the last bus, so their father collected them. Pablo enjoyed the evening, but next time he wants to check the bus times first.

reading.why: La hermana sugiere phone case y tiene razón.
Their father collected them.

dialogue: What did you do last weekend?
I went to a concert with my sister.
Yes, but I almost lost my ticket.
My father collected us because we missed the bus.
units.writing: Escribe 60–80 palabras sobre un día memorable. Incluye cuándo, dónde, con quién, tres hechos y cómo te sentiste. Usa al menos dos conectores.
units.model: Last Sunday morning, I visited a small museum with my brother. First, we bought our tickets and looked at some old photographs. Then we joined a short tour. The guide told us an interesting story about our town. After that, we had lunch in a café. I felt happy because I learned something new and spent time with my brother.

listening.text: Hi Mia. Yesterday I left my umbrella on the bus. I called the transport office this morning. They found it and said I can collect it tomorrow before five. The office is next to the station. I am glad because the umbrella was a present from my grandmother.

questions.why: Dice Yesterday I left my umbrella.

questions.answer: Fue un regalo de su abuela.
options: Fue un regalo de su abuela.
Es el único objeto de su bolsa.
questions.why: Dice a present from my grandmother.

units.mission: Cuenta una historia de un minuto siguiendo First, then y finally. Tu compañero hace dos preguntas con did.

units.title: Lo que estaba pasando
units.en: In the middle of a story
units.goal: Describir acciones en curso en el pasado y relacionarlas con acontecimientos.

rules.title: Una acción en desarrollo
rules.text: Past continuous se forma con was/were + -ing. Describe lo que estaba ocurriendo alrededor de un momento pasado, sin enfocar el inicio ni el final. Usa was con I/he/she/it y were con you/we/they. Para preguntar, coloca was/were antes del sujeto.
rules.pattern: At eight, I was cooking.
examples: I was reading at nine last night.
They were waiting outside the café.
What were you doing at six?
rules.tip: Elige was o were según el sujeto, no según el verbo que termina en -ing.

rules.title: Fondo y acontecimiento
rules.text: Combina past continuous para la acción en curso y past simple para un acontecimiento que ocurrió durante ella. When suele introducir el acontecimiento; while suele introducir una acción en desarrollo. La forma verbal depende del significado, no de memorizar que una palabra obliga siempre a usar un tiempo.
rules.pattern: I was walking when it started to rain.
examples: We were eating when the lights went out.
While I was studying, my phone rang.
She fell while she was running.
rules.tip: La acción breve no necesita llevar -ing: rang marca el acontecimiento.

rules.title: Dos acciones y detalles
rules.text: Usa dos formas continuas para acciones simultáneas: while I was cooking, he was reading. Añade detalles del lugar y el clima para que el oyente imagine la escena. Termina con una acción en past simple y una reacción. No uses normalmente continuo con estados como know o want.
rules.pattern: While I was…, she was…
examples: While I was cooking, my sister was reading.
It was raining and people were running.
In the end, we stayed at home.
rules.tip: Para decir no lo sabía usa I did not know, no I was not knowing.

questions.prompt: What ___ you doing when I called?
questions.why: Were introduce la pregunta en continuo.

questions.prompt: I was sleeping when the phone ___.
questions.why: Rang es el acontecimiento que interrumpe.

questions.prompt: While she ___, she saw an old friend.
questions.why: Was walking presenta la acción en curso.

questions.prompt: I was cooking while Leo ___ the table.
questions.why: Las dos acciones se desarrollaban a la vez.

questions.prompt: Elige la forma habitual: No lo sabía.

units.story: Yesterday evening, there was a power cut in our street. I was doing my homework and my parents were preparing dinner when the lights went out. At first, we could not see anything. My father found a torch and my mother looked for candles. Outside, it was raining heavily. While we were sitting in the kitchen, someone knocked on the door. It was our neighbour, who needed help with her phone. We invited her in and shared some cold food. The electricity came back an hour later. We did not finish our usual evening plans, but we enjoyed talking without the television.

reading.prompt: ¿Qué hacía el narrador cuando se apagó la luz?
reading.why: I was doing my homework.
Invitaron a la vecina y comieron juntos.

dialogue: What were you doing when the lights went out?
Our neighbour came in and we shared some food.
units.writing: Escribe 60–80 palabras sobre una interrupción. Describe dos acciones en curso, qué ocurrió y cómo terminó la situación.
units.model: I was walking home yesterday when it started to rain. Some children were playing in the park, and they ran towards the entrance. I did not have an umbrella, so I waited in a small shop. While I was waiting, I called my sister. She came to collect me twenty minutes later. In the end, we bought hot chocolate and went home together.

listening.text: At half past eight yesterday, I was cycling to work. A dog suddenly ran across the road, so I stopped. I did not fall, but my bag fell onto the ground. A woman who was walking nearby helped me pick up my things. Luckily, nothing was broken.

questions.why: Dice my bag fell; I did not fall.

units.mission: Mira por una ventana e imagina la escena ayer: di tres acciones en curso. Añade un acontecimiento con when y cuenta cómo terminó.

units.title: Experiencias de vida
units.goal: Preguntar por experiencias sin fecha y responder con detalles en pasado.

rules.title: Experiencias hasta ahora
rules.text: Present perfect se forma con have/has + participio. Sirve para hablar de experiencias anteriores conectadas con la vida hasta ahora cuando no dices un momento pasado terminado. Los regulares usan -ed; algunos participios son irregulares: been, seen, eaten, ridden. Para una fecha concreta usa past simple.
rules.pattern: I have visited… / She has seen…
examples: I have visited another country.
She has ridden a horse.
We have tried Japanese food.
rules.tip: No digas I have visited Lima yesterday: yesterday pide past simple en este uso.

rules.title: Ever, never y respuestas
rules.text: Ever suele aparecer en preguntas sobre si algo ocurrió alguna vez. Never significa nunca y se coloca entre have/has y el participio, sin not adicional. Responde Yes, I have o No, I haven’t. Para pedir detalles cambia a past simple: When did you go?
rules.pattern: Have you ever…? / I have never…
examples: Have you ever slept in a tent?
I have never won a prize.
Yes, I have, but only once.
rules.tip: Después de have no uses directamente el pasado went: usa been o gone según el sentido.

rules.title: Been, gone y seguimiento
rules.text: Has been to describe una visita de la que la persona ya volvió. Has gone to indica que se fue y aún no ha regresado. Una conversación natural pasa del present perfect al past simple para contar dónde, cuándo y con quién. Puedes usar once, twice y several times para contar experiencias.
rules.pattern: She has been to… / She has gone to…
examples: My brother has been to Chile twice.
Ana has gone to the supermarket.
I went there with my family last year.
rules.tip: Been to y gone to no dicen lo mismo sobre dónde está ahora la persona.

questions.why: El participio de ride es ridden.

questions.prompt: Leo is back home. He has ___ to Peru.
___ did you visit the city? — Last year.
questions.why: Para una fecha concreta se pregunta con past simple.

units.story: Our English club is collecting interesting experiences. Sofia has ridden a horse, but she has never climbed a mountain. She rode a horse for the first time during a family holiday two years ago. Mateo has been to three countries and has tried many different kinds of food. His favourite trip was to Peru, where he visited his uncle last summer. I have never travelled abroad, but I have slept in a tent near the coast. It was cold and windy, and I did not sleep very well. We all agreed that an experience does not have to be expensive or far away to be interesting.

reading.why: Se dice explícitamente que Sofia nunca lo ha hecho.

reading.answer: Una experiencia cercana puede ser interesante.
options: Una experiencia cercana puede ser interesante.
Solo los viajes caros son interesantes.
Dormir en una tienda siempre es cómodo.
reading.why: La última frase rechaza que deba ser cara o lejana.

dialogue: Have you ever slept in a tent?
Yes, I have. I did it last summer.
I went to the coast with my cousins.
Would you like to do it again?
Yes, but next time I want a warmer sleeping bag.
units.writing: Escribe 60–80 palabras: dos experiencias que has tenido, una que no has tenido y detalles de una experiencia con fecha terminada.
units.model: I have visited several interesting museums, and I have tried food from different countries. However, I have never travelled abroad. Last month, I went to a science museum with my class. We saw an exhibition about space and made a small paper rocket. I enjoyed the visit because I learned a lot. I would like to visit another museum soon.

listening.text: Welcome to our travel club. You do not need to have travelled abroad to join us. I have been to the mountains several times, but my favourite trip was to a lake last May. Next week, Sara will talk about her first train journey. Please bring one photo of a place you have visited.

questions.why: You do not need to have travelled abroad.
My favourite trip was to a lake.

questions.answer: Una foto de un lugar visitado.
options: Una foto de un lugar visitado.

units.mission: Haz tres preguntas con Have you ever…? Después de cada sí, pide detalles con When, Where o Who en pasado.

units.title: Noticias y cambios recientes
units.goal: Expresar resultados actuales, tareas pendientes y duración con present perfect.

rules.title: Just, already y yet
rules.text: Con present perfect, just indica algo muy reciente y already algo que ocurrió antes de ahora o de lo esperado. Suelen ir entre have/has y el participio. Yet suele ir al final de preguntas y negativas para algo esperado. En inglés estadounidense también es frecuente past simple con just; aquí practicamos el patrón con perfect.
rules.pattern: I have just… / Have you… yet?
examples: I have just sent the email.
She has already finished her homework.
We have not booked the tickets yet.
rules.tip: Yet en una pregunta puede equivaler a ya: Have you eaten yet?

rules.title: For y since
rules.text: For introduce una duración: for two years. Since introduce el punto inicial: since 2024, since Monday. Present perfect permite expresar situaciones que empezaron antes y continúan ahora. How long have you lived here? pregunta la duración. Con be se usa been: I have been here for an hour.
rules.pattern: have/has + participio + for/since
examples: I have lived here for three years.
She has known him since primary school.
How long have you had this phone?
rules.tip: No traduzcas literalmente llevo tres años viviendo aquí como I have three years here.

rules.title: Perfect o pasado terminado
rules.text: Usa past simple si el momento está terminado y definido: yesterday, in 2020. Usa present perfect para resultados actuales o un periodo considerado abierto: so far, today si el día sigue. La elección depende del contexto. Pregunta Have you finished? y luego When did you finish? para precisar.
rules.pattern: I have lost it. / I lost it yesterday.
examples: I have lost my keys and cannot get in.
I lost my old phone last year.
We have completed two tasks so far.
rules.tip: No combines normalmente present perfect con ago o last week.

questions.prompt: I have ___ finished lunch. It was a minute ago.

questions.why: Yet suele ir al final de la pregunta.

questions.prompt: We have lived here ___ six months.

questions.why: So far relaciona el resultado con ahora.

units.story: Hi Laura, we have finally moved into our new flat. We have lived here for two weeks, and we already know some of our neighbours. My father has painted the kitchen, but we have not bought a new table yet. I have just put my books on a shelf in my bedroom. I lost my favourite notebook during the move, but I found it yesterday in a box of shoes. The flat is smaller than our old house, but it is closer to school. I have walked to school every day since Monday. Would you like to visit us this weekend? We can make lunch together.

reading.why: They have not bought a new table yet.
Every day since Monday.

dialogue: Yes, we have, but we have not bought all the furniture.
How long have you lived there?
We have lived there for two weeks.
Yes, I have just spoken to the family next door.
units.writing: Escribe un mensaje de 60–80 palabras sobre un cambio reciente. Incluye algo ya terminado, algo pendiente y una duración con for o since.
units.model: Hi Alex, I have just joined a new English club. I have been a member for two weeks, and I have already met some friendly people. We have finished our first group project, but we have not presented it yet. I joined because I wanted more speaking practice. The next meeting is on Friday. Would you like to come with me?

listening.text: Hello, this is the repair shop. We have fixed your laptop, but we have not received the new charger yet. It should arrive tomorrow. You can collect the laptop today if you bring your old charger. We have been open since nine, and we close at half past five.

questions.why: We have not received the new charger yet.

units.mission: Cuenta tres novedades con just, already y yet. Pregunta How long have you…? y responde con for o since.

units.title: Planes y predicciones
units.goal: Distinguir intenciones, decisiones inmediatas, predicciones y planes acordados.

rules.title: Going to: intención y evidencia
rules.text: Be going to + verbo base expresa una intención previa o una predicción basada en evidencia visible. Mantén am/is/are en preguntas y negativas. No lo confundas con go to + lugar: I am going to Lima describe un desplazamiento; I am going to study describe un plan.
rules.pattern: am/is/are going to + verbo
examples: I am going to learn to swim.
Look at those clouds. It is going to rain.
Are you going to call your cousin?
rules.tip: Después de going to usa el verbo base, no -ing.

rules.title: Will: decisión, oferta y predicción
rules.text: Will + verbo base sirve para una decisión tomada al hablar, una oferta, promesa o predicción. La contracción negativa es won’t. La forma no cambia con el sujeto. I think y probably expresan que una predicción no es segura. Elige la forma por el contexto, no solo porque menciona el futuro.
rules.pattern: I will help. / It will probably…
examples: Your bag is heavy. I will carry it.
I think the team will win.
I will not forget your birthday.
rules.tip: No añadas -s después de will: she will comes es incorrecto.

rules.title: Present continuous: plan acordado
rules.text: Un plan concreto ya organizado puede expresarse con present continuous y una referencia futura: I am meeting Ana tomorrow. Suele implicar hora, lugar o acuerdo con alguien. Contrasta intención general, plan acordado y decisión inmediata. Una misma situación puede admitir más de una forma según qué quieras destacar.
rules.pattern: I am meeting… tomorrow at…
examples: We are meeting at the station at ten.
I am seeing the dentist on Tuesday.
What are you doing this weekend?
rules.tip: Incluye contexto futuro para distinguir un plan de una acción que ocurre ahora.

questions.prompt: Ya decidí aprender. I am ___ learn to swim.
Tu amigo no puede abrir la puerta. Ofreces:
questions.why: Will permite ofrecer ayuda al momento.
Will va seguido de verbo base.

questions.prompt: Hay cita confirmada: I ___ the dentist at three tomorrow.
questions.why: El continuo expresa el plan acordado.

units.story: Luis has several plans for next month. He is going to take a swimming course because he wants to feel more confident in the water. He has already booked the lessons, and he is meeting his instructor on Monday at six. His sister thinks the course will be difficult at first, but Luis is not worried. “I will practise,” he says. He is also saving money for a new bicycle. He probably will not buy it this month because he needs to pay for the course first. This evening, he is meeting a friend to discuss a short cycling trip for the summer.

reading.prompt: ¿Qué plan ya tiene una hora acordada?
reading.why: La reunión es el lunes a las seis.

reading.prompt: ¿Por qué probablemente no comprará la bicicleta este mes?
options: No le gusta ir en bicicleta.
reading.why: Necesita pagar las clases primero.

dialogue: What are you going to do next month?
I am going to take a swimming course.
When are you meeting the instructor?
Yes, please. I will be ready at half past five.
units.writing: Escribe 60–80 palabras sobre dos intenciones, un plan acordado y una predicción. Explica al menos una razón.
units.model: Next month, I am going to improve my English and spend more time outside. I am meeting my study partner on Tuesday at four. We have booked a room in the library. At the weekend, I am going to walk with my family. I think these changes will help me feel better. I will probably have less time for video games.

listening.text: Hi Dan. We are meeting outside the cinema at seven tomorrow. I am going to buy the tickets online tonight. The film starts at half past seven and lasts ninety minutes. I think you will enjoy it. If you arrive early, I will meet you in the café next door.

questions.why: Meeting at seven; la película empieza después.

units.mission: Explica tres planes usando going to, un encuentro con present continuous y una predicción con will. Pide a alguien una sugerencia.

units.title: Invitaciones y citas
units.goal: Invitar, aceptar, rechazar con cortesía y cambiar una cita.

rules.title: Invitar y sugerir
rules.text: Would you like to + verbo es una invitación cortés. Let’s + verbo propone hacer algo juntos. How about y What about pueden ir con un nombre o con -ing. Why don’t we + verbo también propone una actividad. Responde mostrando interés y acuerda los detalles.
rules.pattern: Would you like to…? / How about…ing?
examples: Would you like to have lunch with us?
Let us meet outside the library.
How about going to the park?
rules.tip: Después de would like se usa to; después de how about, -ing.

rules.title: Aceptar o rechazar
rules.text: Para aceptar usa I’d love to, That sounds good o Yes, please según el contexto. Para rechazar sin sonar brusco, agradece y da una razón breve: I’d love to, but I’m working. Puedes ofrecer otra fecha con instead. No necesitas inventar una excusa larga para ser cortés.
rules.pattern: I would love to, but…
examples: That sounds great. What time shall we meet?
I would love to, but I am working.
Can we meet on Sunday instead?
rules.tip: I like to habla de gustos habituales; I would like to expresa un deseo o invitación actual.

rules.title: Precisar y cambiar la hora
rules.text: Usa at con horas, on con días y fechas, in con meses o partes del día. Tomorrow no necesita preposición. From…to… delimita un intervalo. Para cambiar una cita di el cambio, comprueba disponibilidad y confirma hora y lugar. Repeat that y Do you mean…? ayudan a evitar errores.
rules.pattern: Are you free on… at…?
examples: Are you free on Friday at three?
The office is open from nine to five.
Could we change the appointment to Monday?
rules.tip: At night es una expresión fija; por la mañana suele ser in the morning.

questions.prompt: Would you like ___ dinner with us?
questions.why: Would like va con to + verbo.

questions.answer: I would love to, but can we meet on Sunday?
options: I would love to, but can we meet on Sunday?
questions.why: Agradece la invitación y ofrece otra fecha.
On para día y at para hora.

questions.answer: Do you mean fifteen or fifty?
options: Do you mean fifteen or fifty?
questions.why: Do you mean…? comprueba qué se ha dicho.

units.story: Hi Chloe, thanks for inviting me to your birthday picnic on Saturday. I would love to come, but I have a dentist’s appointment in the morning. I should be free after twelve. Is that too late? I can bring sandwiches and some fruit. I know that you wanted to meet near the lake, but the weather forecast says it may rain. How about meeting at your house instead if the weather is bad? Please let me know what you think. Also, could you send me your address again? I remember the street, but I have forgotten the house number. See you soon, Nina.

reading.prompt: ¿Por qué Nina no puede ir por la mañana?
reading.why: Tiene una dentist’s appointment.
Sugiere meeting at your house instead.

dialogue: Would you like to join us on Saturday?
I would love to, but I am busy until twelve.
That is fine. Shall we meet at one?
At my house. Could you bring some fruit?
Of course. Please send me your address.
units.writing: Responde a una invitación en 60–80 palabras. Agradece, acepta o rechaza con una razón, propone hora y pregunta un detalle.
units.model: Hi Eva, thank you for inviting me to your lunch on Sunday. I would love to come. I am visiting my grandparents in the morning, so can I arrive at one? I can bring some juice and a cake. Are we eating outside or in your kitchen? Please send me your address because I have never been to your new house.

listening.text: Good afternoon. I am calling about your appointment with Mr Green on Thursday. We need to change it from eleven to half past twelve. If that time does not suit you, we can offer Friday at nine. Please call us before five today to confirm your choice.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál era la hora original del jueves?

units.mission: Con otra persona organiza una salida: invitación, primer horario no disponible, alternativa y confirmación de hora y lugar.

units.title: Comparar opciones
units.goal: Comparar personas, lugares y servicios con razones.

rules.title: Comparativos
rules.text: Adjetivos cortos suelen añadir -er: cheaper, bigger. Los terminados en consonante + y cambian a -ier: easier. Los más largos suelen usar more: more comfortable. Añade than para mencionar la otra opción. Good y bad son irregulares: better y worse. Much y a bit pueden indicar la magnitud de la diferencia.
rules.pattern: A is cheaper than B.
examples: The bus is cheaper than the taxi.
This room is more comfortable than that one.
The new route is a bit faster.
rules.tip: No combines more y -er: more cheaper es incorrecto.

rules.title: Superlativos
rules.text: El superlativo compara con todo un grupo: the cheapest, the most interesting. Good se convierte en the best y bad en the worst. Delimita el grupo con in o of: in our town, of the three. Usa one of the + superlativo + nombre plural para destacar un miembro de un grupo.
rules.pattern: the + -est / most + adjetivo
examples: This is the cheapest café in town.
It is one of the most beautiful parks.
That was the best part of the trip.
rules.tip: Después de one of the… el nombre suele ir en plural.

rules.title: Igualdad y diferencias
rules.text: As + adjetivo + as expresa igualdad. Not as…as indica menor grado. Usa la forma básica del adjetivo, no el comparativo. Para comparar gustos añade I prefer A because…; una opción puede ser mejor en precio y peor en distancia. Así justificas una decisión con más de un criterio.
rules.pattern: as comfortable as / not as quiet as
examples: The train is as fast as the bus today.
This hotel is not as quiet as the other one.
I prefer this café because it is closer.
rules.tip: Not as expensive as significa que cuesta menos, no más.

questions.prompt: This exercise is ___ than the first one.
The sofa is ___ than that chair.
questions.why: Comfortable forma el comparativo con more.

questions.prompt: It is ___ restaurant in the village.
questions.why: Se compara con todo el grupo.

questions.prompt: One of the tallest ___ is near the river.
This room is as ___ as yours.
A is not as expensive as B. ¿Cuál cuesta menos?
questions.why: A tiene un grado menor de expensive.

units.story: We need to choose a place for our study group. The library is the quietest option, but it closes at five. The café is open later and has more comfortable chairs, although it is usually crowded after school. My house is not as large as the café, but it is much closer to everyone’s home. We can also use the community centre. It costs a little money, but it has the biggest table and the fastest internet connection. In the end, we chose the library for short meetings and my house for longer ones. The best choice depends on what we need that day.

reading.prompt: ¿Cuál es el inconveniente de la biblioteca?
reading.why: The library closes at five.

reading.answer: Usar dos lugares según la reunión.
options: Usar dos lugares según la reunión.
reading.why: Biblioteca para reuniones cortas y casa para largas.

dialogue: The smaller one. It is cheaper and quieter.
Is it as close to the station as the other one?
No, but it is only ten minutes away.
It has the most comfortable beds.
units.writing: Compara dos lugares en 60–80 palabras: precio o tamaño, comodidad y distancia. Usa un comparativo, un superlativo y as…as.
units.model: There are two small cafés near my school. The Green Café is cheaper than the Blue Café, but it is not as comfortable. The Blue Café has the best sandwiches in the area and larger tables. However, it is often crowded. I prefer the Green Café for studying because it is quieter in the afternoon and closer to my house.

listening.text: We have three bicycles for rent. The city bike is the cheapest at eight pounds a day. The mountain bike costs twelve pounds and is better for rough paths. The electric bike is the most expensive at twenty pounds. All three are available until six this evening.

units.mission: Elige entre dos medios de transporte usando tres criterios. Tu compañero propone otra opción y tú explicas cuál prefieres.

units.title: Comida y cantidades
units.goal: Pedir cantidades, leer una receta y hablar de hábitos alimentarios.

rules.title: Contables e incontables
rules.text: Contables admiten número y plural: two apples. Incontables como rice, flour, advice o information no suelen tener plural en estos usos. Usa unidades: a bag of rice, two pieces of information. Much pregunta cantidad incontable y many cantidad contable. A lot of sirve con ambos.
rules.pattern: How much rice? / How many apples?
examples: We need a bottle of oil.
How many eggs are there?
There is a lot of rice in the cupboard.
rules.tip: No digas two breads para dos piezas comunes: usa two loaves o two slices según lo que quieres.

rules.title: A few y a little
rules.text: A few acompaña a contables plurales; a little, a incontables. Ambos indican una cantidad pequeña pero existente. Few y little sin a suelen destacar que la cantidad es insuficiente. Some aparece en afirmaciones y ofertas; any es frecuente en preguntas generales y negativas.
rules.pattern: a few tomatoes / a little milk
examples: We have a few tomatoes left.
Add a little milk to the sauce.
Would you like some water?
rules.tip: Some también es normal al ofrecer o pedir algo que esperas que esté disponible.

rules.title: Too much y enough
rules.text: Too much con incontables y too many con plurales indican exceso. Enough va antes de un nombre: enough food. Las recetas usan imperativos: chop, mix, boil, add. First, then y finally ordenan los pasos. Repite cantidades y tiempos para comprobar que entendiste las instrucciones.
rules.pattern: too much salt / enough vegetables
examples: There is too much salt in this soup.
We have enough food for six people.
First chop the onions, then mix the ingredients.
rules.tip: Enough antes del nombre, pero después de un adjetivo: hot enough.

questions.prompt: We have ___ apples, so we can make a small pie.

questions.why: Enough va antes de un plural contable.

units.story: On Sunday, our family decided to make vegetable soup. We had a few carrots and some potatoes, but there were not enough onions. My brother went to the shop while I washed the vegetables. First, we chopped everything into small pieces. Then we heated a little oil in a large pan and added the onions. After a few minutes, we added the other vegetables and some water. My father wanted to add more salt, but the soup already had enough. We cooked it for twenty minutes and served it with bread. There was enough soup for everyone, and we saved two portions for Monday.

reading.why: No había suficientes onions.

options: La llevaron al colegio ese día.
reading.why: Saved two portions for Monday.

dialogue: Have we got enough food for the picnic?
We have a few sandwiches, but not much fruit.
Six. We need some more apples.
Shall I buy a bottle of water too?
Yes, please. There is only a little water left.
units.writing: Escribe una receta sencilla de 60–80 palabras con ingredientes, cantidades y cuatro pasos. Incluye enough, a few o a little.
units.model: To make a simple salad, you need a few tomatoes, one cucumber, a little oil and some cheese. First, wash the vegetables carefully. Then cut them into small pieces and put them in a bowl. Add the cheese and a little oil. Finally, mix everything together. Do not add too much salt. This recipe makes enough salad for two people.

listening.text: For today’s cooking class, bring two eggs, a small bag of flour and a bottle of water. You do not need to bring oil because we have enough. Please arrive at ten. We will make lunch together, and the class will finish at half past twelve.

units.mission: Planea comida para cuatro personas. Pregunta qué hay, identifica dos ingredientes que faltan y explica una receta en cuatro pasos.

units.title: Compras y devoluciones
units.goal: Elegir productos, pedir tallas y explicar un problema con una compra.

rules.title: One y ones para no repetir
rules.text: One sustituye un nombre contable singular y ones uno plural: the blue one, the smaller ones. No sustituyen directamente incontables como milk en estos usos. Which one? pide elegir entre opciones conocidas. This one y those ones pueden señalar productos en una tienda.
rules.pattern: the blue one / the smaller ones
examples: I prefer the blue one.
Do you have any smaller ones?
Which one would you like to try on?
rules.tip: Después de a/an, un adjetivo + one puede sustituir el nombre: a cheaper one.

rules.title: Too y enough con adjetivos
rules.text: Too + adjetivo indica un exceso que crea un problema: too small. Adjetivo + enough indica suficiencia: large enough. Very solo intensifica y no implica necesariamente un problema. Puedes añadir to + verbo: comfortable enough to wear all day. Relaciona tu evaluación con la finalidad.
rules.pattern: too small / big enough
examples: These shoes are too small.
This bag is not large enough.
The jacket is warm enough for winter.
rules.tip: No digas enough big: con adjetivos se coloca después.

rules.title: Explicar y pedir una solución
rules.text: Para una devolución, indica qué compraste y cuándo en past simple, explica el problema y pide una solución con could o would like. Have you got the receipt? es una pregunta habitual. Las condiciones reales dependen de cada tienda; aquí practicamos lenguaje, no derechos de devolución.
rules.pattern: I bought… / Could I exchange it?
examples: I bought this shirt yesterday.
Could I exchange it for a larger size?
I would like a refund, please.
rules.tip: Try it on separa el verbo con un pronombre: no try on it.

questions.prompt: I like the red shoes. Have you got smaller ___?
Which ___ do you prefer: this coat or that coat?
This box is ___ heavy for me to carry.
questions.why: Too heavy expresa un exceso problemático.
Try on se separa cuando el objeto es un pronombre.

questions.prompt: Petición cortés para cambiar una prenda:
questions.why: Could I…? formula la petición con cortesía.

units.story: Maya bought a pair of shoes online last week. They looked comfortable in the photos, but when they arrived, they were too small. She checked the information in the box and took them to the shop with her receipt. The assistant asked if she wanted a refund or an exchange. Maya liked the shoes, so she asked for a larger size. The shop did not have the same colour, but there was a black pair. She tried them on and walked around for a minute. The black ones fitted well, and they were cheaper too. Maya left the shop with comfortable shoes and a small refund.

reading.why: They were too small.
The black ones fitted well.

dialogue: Yes. I bought these shoes yesterday, but they are too small.
Yes, here it is. Could I exchange them?
Of course. Would you like to try these ones on?
Yes, please. They look more comfortable.
units.writing: Escribe a una tienda en 60–80 palabras: producto, fecha de compra, problema y solución que solicitas. Mantén un tono cortés.
units.model: Hello, I bought a bright blue backpack from your website last Tuesday. It arrived yesterday, but one of the pockets is broken. The bag is the right size, so I would prefer an exchange rather than a refund. I still have the original receipt and the box. Could you tell me how to return it? Thank you for your help.

listening.text: Good morning. Our summer sale starts today. All T-shirts are eight pounds, and you can buy two for fourteen pounds. The changing rooms are at the back of the shop. Please keep your receipt if you may want to exchange an item. We close at seven today.

questions.why: At the back of the shop.

units.mission: Representa una compra: pide otro color, prueba una talla, explica por qué no sirve y solicita una alternativa.

units.title: Moverte por la ciudad
units.goal: Comprender indicaciones, localizar servicios y describir tu barrio.

rules.title: Posición y movimiento
rules.text: Opposite indica enfrente, next to al lado y between entre dos referencias. Para movimiento usa across the road, along the street, past the bank o through the park. To indica destino y towards dirección general. Combina una referencia conocida con un paso breve para orientar a alguien.
rules.pattern: Go past… / Turn left at…
examples: Walk along this street.
The bank is opposite the library.
Go past the café and turn right.
rules.tip: Across cruza de un lado a otro; along sigue el recorrido.

rules.title: Lugares con where
rules.text: Where une un lugar con lo que sucede allí: the café where we meet. Who identifica personas; that/which pueden identificar cosas. No repitas una referencia al lugar innecesariamente: the park where we play, no where we play there. Este recurso permite explicar una palabra que no conoces.
rules.pattern: a place where people…
examples: This is the café where we usually meet.
A library is a place where people borrow books.
The shop that sells bikes is next to the station.
rules.tip: Where ya aporta la relación con el lugar.

rules.title: Pedir y verificar indicaciones
rules.text: Comienza con Excuse me. Could you tell me the way to…? pide ayuda. How far is it? pregunta distancia y How long does it take? duración. Para confirmar, repite los pasos: So I turn left at the bank? Divide las instrucciones en dos o tres pasos cada vez.
rules.pattern: How far…? / How long does it take?
examples: Excuse me, how do I get to the museum?
Is it within walking distance?
So I turn left at the traffic lights?
rules.tip: Escucha las referencias y confirma izquierda/derecha; no basta con reconocer cada palabra aislada.

questions.prompt: Cruza la carretera: Walk ___ the road.
questions.why: Across indica de un lado al otro.

questions.prompt: El banco está enfrente: The bank is ___ the café.
This is the park ___ we play football.
questions.why: Where une un lugar y la actividad.

questions.prompt: The shop ___ sells bread opens at six.
questions.why: That actúa como sujeto de sells.

questions.answer: So I turn right after the bank?
options: So I turn right after the bank?

units.story: Our neighbourhood has changed a lot. There is now a small library opposite the sports centre, and a café has opened next to the station. The library is the place where I meet my study group every Wednesday. To get there from the station, walk along King Street and go past the supermarket. Turn left at the traffic lights. You will see the sports centre on your right and the library on your left. It takes about ten minutes on foot. There is also a bus, but walking is usually faster because the roads are busy in the afternoon. The library entrance is beside a large tree.

reading.why: La biblioteca está opposite the sports centre.

reading.answer: Es más rápido con el tráfico de la tarde.
options: Es más rápido con el tráfico de la tarde.
reading.why: Walking is usually faster because roads are busy.

dialogue: Excuse me, how do I get to the library?
Walk along this street and go past the supermarket.
Do I turn at the traffic lights?
Yes, turn left. The library is opposite the sports centre.
How long does it take on foot?
About ten minutes. The entrance is beside a big tree.
units.writing: Describe tu barrio y cómo llegar a un lugar en 60–80 palabras. Incluye tres pasos, dos referencias y una oración con where.
units.model: There is a small park near my house where people walk and play games. To get there from the bus stop, walk along Green Street and go past the bakery. Turn right at the bank. The park is opposite the school, and its entrance is next to a café. It takes about five minutes on foot. I often meet my friends there.

listening.text: For the community centre, get off at the next bus stop. Cross the road at the traffic lights and walk past the pharmacy. Turn right after the pharmacy. The centre is the second building on your left, opposite a small park. Use the side entrance today because the front entrance is closed.

questions.why: Get off at the next bus stop.

units.mission: Dibuja un mapa sencillo con cinco lugares. Da indicaciones sin señalar el destino y comprueba si otra persona llega al lugar correcto.

units.title: Viajes y transporte
units.goal: Consultar horarios, comprar billetes y comprender cambios de viaje.

rules.title: Horarios en present simple
rules.text: Los horarios establecidos suelen expresarse con present simple aunque se refieran al futuro: The train leaves at six tomorrow. Para preguntar usa does con sujeto singular. By indica un límite máximo de tiempo; until indica que algo continúa hasta ese momento. Comprueba fecha, hora y destino por separado.
rules.pattern: What time does… leave?
examples: The train leaves at half past six.
What time does the bus arrive?
Please be at the station by six.
rules.tip: By six = a más tardar a las seis; until six = hasta las seis.

rules.title: Billetes y transporte
rules.text: Pide un single o return ticket e indica destino y fecha. How much is…? pregunta precio. Con medios de transporte suele usarse by sin artículo: by bus, by train; on foot para a pie. Get on/off se usa con bus y train; get in/out of con car o taxi.
rules.pattern: A return ticket to…, please.
examples: I usually travel by train.
We got off the bus at the station.
How much is a return ticket to Oxford?
rules.tip: Luggage es incontable: usa a piece of luggage, no a luggage.

rules.title: Anuncios y problemas
rules.text: Un anuncio puede cambiar un dato ya conocido: andén, horario o destino. Escucha la información final, no solo el primer número. Usa Could you repeat that? y Does this train stop at…? para confirmar. Si pierdes un servicio, explica en past simple y pregunta por el siguiente.
rules.pattern: The service is delayed. / Which platform?
examples: Our train is delayed by twenty minutes.
Does this train stop at Central Station?
I missed my bus. When is the next one?
rules.tip: Delayed by twenty minutes significa veinte minutos de retraso, no necesariamente salida a las veinte.

questions.prompt: The train ___ at eight tomorrow morning.

questions.answer: Llega a más tardar a las diez.
options: Llega a más tardar a las diez.

questions.why: By bus sin artículo describe el medio.

questions.prompt: Get ___ the train at the next station.
questions.why: Se usa get off con train.

questions.prompt: Sale a las 10:00 y tiene 20 minutos de retraso. ¿Nueva hora?
questions.why: Añade veinte minutos a la hora prevista.
Return ticket incluye los dos trayectos.

units.story: Rosa and her brother planned to visit their grandparents by train. Their train was due to leave at ten, so they arrived at the station at half past nine. Rosa bought two return tickets and checked the departure board. At first, the train was listed at platform three, but an announcement changed it to platform five. Then another message said it was delayed by fifteen minutes. They used the extra time to buy some water. When the train arrived, they found seats near the window. The journey took forty minutes, and their grandfather was waiting at the station. They returned home on the last train that evening.

reading.why: El anuncio cambia el andén de tres a cinco.
The journey took forty minutes.

dialogue: A return ticket to Central Station, please.
Yes. What time does the next train leave?
At ten fifteen, from platform five.
Do I need to change trains?
No, it is a direct service.
units.writing: Escribe 60–80 palabras a alguien que te recogerá: medio de transporte, salida, llegada, posible cambio y punto de encuentro.
units.model: Hi Tom, I am travelling by train tomorrow. My train leaves at nine and arrives at Central Station at ten forty. I have a small bag, so I can walk easily. Could we meet outside the main entrance? If the train is delayed, I will send you a message. Thank you for meeting me. I am looking forward to seeing you.

listening.text: Attention, passengers. The ten thirty service to Westford will now depart from platform four, not platform two. The service is delayed by ten minutes and will leave at ten forty. Please keep your luggage with you. Passengers for Eastford should wait for the next service.

questions.prompt: ¿De qué andén sale el tren a Westford?
questions.why: El dato final es platform four.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué deben hacer los viajeros a Eastford?
questions.why: Should wait for the next service.

units.mission: Representa la compra de dos billetes. Confirma precio, horario, andén y si hay transbordo. Después explica un retraso a quien te espera.

units.title: Alojamiento y peticiones
units.goal: Reservar alojamiento, pedir servicios y explicar problemas con cortesía.

rules.title: Pedir con can y could
rules.text: Can you…? y Could you…? piden que alguien haga algo; could suele sonar más cortés. Can I…? y Could I…? piden permiso o un servicio para ti. Would like + nombre o to + verbo expresa lo que deseas. Usa please y un tono amable.
rules.pattern: Could you bring…? / Could I have…?
examples: Could I have an extra towel, please?
Could you check the heating?
I would like to book a double room.
rules.tip: En Could you help me now?, could no señala necesariamente el pasado.

rules.title: Describir lo que no funciona
rules.text: Usa present simple para una característica o regla y present continuous para un problema actual: The shower is not working. There is/are presenta lo que hay o falta. Conecta el problema y el efecto: The room is cold, so we need a blanket. Explica el hecho sin exagerarlo.
rules.pattern: There is a problem with…
examples: There is a problem with the shower.
The key card is not working.
There are not enough towels in the room.
rules.tip: No traduzcas hay con have: usa there is/are.

rules.title: Confirmar una reserva
rules.text: En una reserva especifica fechas, número de noches, personas y tipo de habitación. Pregunta si el precio incluye desayuno y la hora de salida. Inclusive significa con algo incluido; no presupongas servicios. Repite los datos clave y pide confirmación por escrito.
rules.pattern: Is breakfast included? / What time is check-out?
examples: I have a booking for two nights.
Is breakfast included in the price?
Could you confirm the booking by email?
rules.tip: Una double room suele tener una cama doble; una twin room, dos camas separadas.

questions.prompt: Petición cortés para recibir una manta:
questions.answer: Could I have a blanket, please?
options: Could I have a blanket, please?

questions.why: Twin room suele referirse a dos camas.
Included indica que forma parte del precio.

units.story: Dear Riverside Hotel, I would like to book a twin room for two nights, from 14 to 16 June. There will be two adults, and we expect to arrive at about eight in the evening. Could you tell me whether breakfast is included in the price? We would also like to know if there is a place to leave our bags after check-out because our train leaves in the afternoon. We do not need a parking space. Please confirm the total price and the latest check-in time by email. Thank you for your help. Best wishes, Adrian Vega.

reading.why: Del 14 al 16 son dos noches.

reading.prompt: ¿Por qué pregunta por dejar las maletas?
reading.answer: Su tren sale por la tarde.
options: Su tren sale por la tarde.
reading.why: Explica que su tren sale después del check-out.

dialogue: Good evening. How can I help you?
I have a booking for two nights under Vega.
Welcome. Here is your key card.
Yes, from seven to ten in the dining room.
Great. Could I also have an extra blanket, please?
units.writing: Escribe una solicitud de reserva de 60–80 palabras con fechas, personas, tipo de habitación y dos preguntas sobre servicios.
units.model: Dear Hill Hotel, I would like to book a double room for two nights, from 8 to 10 August. We are two adults and will arrive at about six in the evening. Is breakfast included in the price? Could you also tell me whether we can leave our bags after check-out? Please send me the total price by email. Thank you for your help.

listening.text: Welcome to Lake House. Breakfast is served from seven thirty to nine thirty. Please leave your room by eleven on your final day. You can leave your bags at reception until six in the evening. If you need an extra towel, call reception by pressing zero on your room phone.

questions.why: From seven thirty to nine thirty.

questions.answer: Hasta las seis de la tarde.
options: Hasta las seis de la tarde.
Hasta las once de la mañana.

questions.why: Pressing zero on the room phone.

units.mission: Explica en recepción que la tarjeta no funciona y falta una toalla. Formula dos peticiones corteses y confirma cuándo recibirás ayuda.

units.title: Bienestar y pedir ayuda
units.goal: Describir síntomas básicos, pedir ayuda y expresar consejos sencillos.

rules.title: Decir cómo te sientes
rules.text: Usa have con problemas: I have a headache. Feel + adjetivo describe el estado: I feel tired. Hurt puede ser verbo: My back hurts. Para duración combina present perfect con for/since: I have had a cough for two days. Este vocabulario sirve para comunicar lo que ocurre a un profesional.
rules.pattern: I have… / I feel… / My… hurts.
examples: I have had a sore throat since Monday.
My knee hurts when I walk.
I feel better today.
rules.tip: I am cold significa que tengo frío; I have a cold, que estoy resfriado.

rules.title: Consejos con should
rules.text: Should/shouldn’t + verbo base formula consejo, no una obligación fuerte. Puedes pedir orientación con What should I do? y añadir una razón. En este curso los consejos son ejemplos lingüísticos generales; la página no evalúa síntomas ni elige tratamientos. Para necesidades concretas, practica cómo pedir atención.
rules.pattern: You should… / You should not…
examples: You should ask for help if you are worried.
You should not ignore the instructions.
What should I do next?
rules.tip: Después de should no añadas to ni -s.

rules.title: Necesidades y preguntas claras
rules.text: Need to expresa necesidad y would like pide un servicio con cortesía. En una cita, describe el problema, cuándo empezó y cómo ha cambiado. Pide que repitan o escriban información que no entiendes. Usa Can you speak more slowly? y Could you write that down? antes de confirmar instrucciones.
rules.pattern: I need to speak to…
examples: I need to speak to a doctor.
Could you write the time down, please?
I would like to make an appointment.
rules.tip: Estas actividades entrenan comunicación, no diagnóstico médico.

questions.prompt: Me duele la espalda: My back ___.
I have had a cough ___ two days.

questions.answer: Could you write it down, please?
options: Could you write it down, please?
questions.why: La petición ayuda a verificar información.

units.story: On Monday, Daniel did not feel well at school. He had a headache and felt very tired. He told his teacher, who helped him call his father. At home, his father asked about the start of the headache, and Daniel explained that it began that morning. They contacted the local health centre to ask for advice. The receptionist offered an appointment later that day. Daniel wrote down the time because he did not want to forget it. By the next morning, he felt better, but he still followed the instructions from the health centre. He was glad that he explained the problem clearly and asked for help.

reading.prompt: ¿A quién contó primero lo que sentía?
reading.why: He told his teacher.
He did not want to forget it.

dialogue: I would like to make an appointment.
What seems to be the problem?
I have had a sore throat for two days.
We have an appointment at three fifteen.
Thank you. Could you repeat the address, please?
units.writing: Escribe un mensaje de 50–70 palabras para justificar una ausencia ficticia y pedir información para recuperar lo trabajado. No necesitas contar datos médicos reales.
units.model: Hello Ms Brown, I cannot come to class today because I do not feel well. I have told my family and asked for help. Could you please tell me which pages the class will study? I would like to catch up when I feel better. I will also ask a classmate for the notes. Thank you for understanding.

listening.text: This is a reminder of your appointment at the health centre tomorrow at quarter past three. Please arrive ten minutes early and bring the letter we sent you. If you cannot attend, call reception before noon tomorrow so we can offer the time to someone else.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué deben hacer si no pueden asistir?
options: Ir al día siguiente sin llamar.

units.mission: Practica una llamada ficticia para pedir una cita: motivo breve, duración, horario y confirmación. No compartas datos sensibles.

units.title: Normas, estudio y trabajo
units.en: What do I have to do?
units.goal: Explicar obligaciones, prohibiciones y tareas que son opcionales.

rules.title: Must y have to
rules.text: Must + verbo base y have to + verbo pueden expresar obligación. Must suele transmitir una norma o una obligación fuerte desde quien habla; have to destaca con frecuencia requisitos externos. Esta distinción no es absoluta. Have to cambia: she has to, we had to. Must no añade -s.
rules.pattern: must do / have to do / has to do
examples: You must wear a helmet here.
She has to arrive before eight.
We had to finish the task yesterday.
rules.tip: Para una obligación pasada usa had to, no musted.

rules.title: Prohibición y falta de obligación
rules.text: Mustn’t significa que algo está prohibido. Don’t/doesn’t have to significa que no es obligatorio, aunque puedes hacerlo. Esta diferencia cambia el sentido de una norma. Can’t también puede expresar prohibición en reglas cotidianas. Explica qué sí se puede hacer como alternativa.
rules.pattern: must not ≠ do not have to
examples: You must not use your phone during the test.
You do not have to bring lunch; it is provided.
She does not have to work on Sundays.
rules.tip: You don’t have to go no significa que tengas prohibido ir.

rules.title: Preguntar por requisitos
rules.text: Do I have to…? consulta una obligación. What do I need to bring? busca requisitos prácticos. Usa by con fechas límite y before para algo anterior. En clase o trabajo, confirma responsable, tarea y fecha. Si hay un problema, avisa y pide ayuda con tiempo.
rules.pattern: Do I have to…? / What do I need to…?
examples: Do I have to wear a uniform?
You need to send the form by Friday.
Could you explain the task again?
rules.tip: Does she have to…? lleva have, no has, después de does.

questions.prompt: She ___ wear a uniform at work.
You must not take photos. Significa…
You do not have to bring lunch. Significa…
questions.why: La ausencia de obligación no es prohibición.
Have to usa do/does en preguntas.

questions.prompt: Send it by Friday. ¿Qué indica by?

units.story: Welcome to your first day at the community library. All volunteers have to arrive ten minutes before their shift so they can prepare the desk. You do not have to wear a uniform, but you should wear comfortable clothes. You must not share visitors’ personal information or leave the front door open after closing time. Lunch is provided on Saturdays, so you do not have to bring food then. If you need to change your shift, please tell the manager by Wednesday. During your first week, an experienced volunteer will work with you and explain how to return books to the correct shelves.

reading.why: You do not have to wear a uniform.
You must not share personal information.

dialogue: Do I have to wear a uniform?
No, but please wear comfortable shoes.
What time do I need to arrive?
Can I change my shift next week?
Yes, but you have to tell the manager by Wednesday.
units.writing: Escribe una guía de 60–80 palabras para alguien nuevo en una clase o actividad. Incluye dos obligaciones, una prohibición y algo opcional.
units.model: Welcome to our art club. You have to arrive at four and help prepare the tables. You must write your name on your work. You must not use someone else’s materials without asking. You do not have to bring paper because the club provides it. Please tell the teacher if you need help. At the end, everyone has to clean their table.

listening.text: For tomorrow’s training day, you need to arrive at the main office by nine. Bring a pen and your identification card. You do not have to bring a laptop because computers are available. Phones must be switched off during the presentation. Lunch is included, and the session finishes at four.

questions.prompt: ¿Cuál es la hora límite de llegada?

questions.why: You do not have to bring a laptop.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué norma se aplica a los teléfonos?
questions.answer: Deben estar apagados durante la presentación.
options: Deben estar apagados durante la presentación.
Hay que dejarlos en casa siempre.

units.mission: Explica a alguien las reglas de una biblioteca o club. Incluye must, mustn’t y don’t have to; pídele que repita la diferencia.

units.title: Capacidades y permiso
units.goal: Hablar de habilidades presentes y pasadas y pedir permiso.

rules.title: Can y could para habilidades
rules.text: Can expresa una habilidad actual y could una habilidad general pasada. La negativa es can’t/couldn’t. Después va el verbo base sin to. Para un logro concreto en una ocasión pasada afirmativa es frecuente was/were able to o managed to; no conviertas automáticamente cualquier pudo en could.
rules.pattern: can now / could when younger
examples: I can repair a bicycle now.
When I was six, I could swim.
We managed to finish before the deadline.
rules.tip: Can no tiene forma infinitiva con to; usa be able to cuando la estructura lo necesite.

rules.title: Permiso, petición y préstamo
rules.text: Can I…? y Could I…? piden permiso; May I…? es más formal. Could you…? pide una acción a otra persona. Borrow significa recibir algo prestado; lend significa dárselo a otra persona por un tiempo. Usa me o you para aclarar quién recibe el objeto.
rules.pattern: Could I borrow…? / Could you lend me…?
examples: Could I borrow your pen?
Could you lend me your notes?
You can use the computer after lunch.
rules.tip: Can I borrow your book? y Can you lend me your book? describen el mismo préstamo desde perspectivas distintas.

rules.title: Modo: cómo haces algo
rules.text: Los adverbios de modo describen cómo se realiza una acción. Muchos añaden -ly: careful → carefully, slow → slowly. Good cambia a well. Fast y hard pueden ser adverbios sin -ly. Colócalos después del verbo o del objeto y úsalos para describir habilidades con más precisión.
rules.pattern: She speaks clearly. / He cooks well.
examples: She explains the rules clearly.
He can play the guitar very well.
Please drive carefully.
rules.tip: Hardly significa casi no; no significa con esfuerzo como hard.

questions.prompt: When I was ten, I ___ ride a bike.
Quieres recibir un libro prestado. Dices…
options: Could I lend your book from you?
Could I borrow you my book?

questions.prompt: Pides que alguien te preste un bolígrafo:
questions.answer: Could you lend me a pen?
options: Could you lend me a pen?
Could you borrow me a pen?
Could you lend I a pen?
questions.why: Lend me indica darme algo prestado.

questions.prompt: She is a good singer. She sings ___.

questions.why: Listen se modifica con el adverbio carefully.

units.story: When Amir was younger, he could draw well, but he could not swim. Last year, he joined a class at the local pool. At first, he felt nervous and moved very slowly. His teacher explained everything clearly and let him practise at his own speed. After several weeks, Amir managed to swim across the small pool without help. Now he can swim confidently, although he still wants to improve. He also helps his friend with drawing. They lend each other materials and share ideas. Amir has learned that being good at one activity does not mean you have to be good at everything immediately.

reading.why: He could draw well.

reading.answer: Cruzar la piscina pequeña sin ayuda.
options: Cruzar la piscina pequeña sin ayuda.
reading.why: Managed to swim across the small pool.

dialogue: Yes, I can. I learned last month.
Could you show me how it works?
Of course. First, open a new document.
Could I borrow your notes too?
Yes, but please return them tomorrow.
units.writing: Escribe 60–80 palabras sobre una habilidad: qué podías hacer antes, qué sabes hacer ahora, cómo aprendiste y qué quieres mejorar.
units.model: When I was younger, I could not cook anything except eggs. Last year, my aunt taught me some really simple recipes. She explained the steps clearly, and I practised every single weekend. Now I can make soup and pasta quite well. Last Sunday, I managed to cook lunch for my family. I still want to learn how to make bread.

listening.text: At our weekend club, you can learn to draw, cook or repair a bicycle. You do not need experience. Please ask before borrowing tools, and return them carefully after use. The drawing class starts at ten, while the bicycle workshop begins at eleven. Places are limited, so book by Thursday.

questions.prompt: ¿Qué deben hacer antes de tomar herramientas?

units.mission: Enseña verbalmente una habilidad en cuatro pasos. Pide un objeto prestado y acuerda cuándo devolverlo.

units.title: Aficiones y decisiones
units.goal: Expresar gustos, objetivos y sugerencias usando formas verbales frecuentes.

rules.title: Verbo + -ing
rules.text: Enjoy y avoid van seguidos de -ing. Después de una preposición, un verbo también suele ir en -ing: interested in learning, good at drawing, instead of watching. Like y love admiten varios patrones; aquí practica like + -ing para actividades. No todas las reglas se deducen del español.
rules.pattern: enjoy doing / interested in doing
examples: I enjoy taking photos.
She is interested in learning to dance.
We went for a walk instead of watching television.
rules.tip: Enjoy to play no es el patrón habitual: enjoy playing.

rules.title: Verbo + to + infinitivo
rules.text: Want, need, decide, hope y would like suelen ir con to + verbo. Learn puede ir con to o how to. Un segundo verbo no lleva automáticamente -ing: hay que aprender el patrón del primero. Escribe tus propios objetivos y la razón para practicarlos.
rules.pattern: want to / decide to / hope to
examples: I want to join a music club.
She decided to learn how to cook.
We hope to visit our cousins soon.
rules.tip: Would like to do expresa un deseo; enjoy doing describe disfrute.

rules.title: Proponer y elegir
rules.text: Para sugerir usa Let’s…, Why don’t we…? o How about…ing? Expresa preferencia con I prefer A to B o I’d rather + verbo base para una elección concreta. Da una razón sencilla con because y acepta otra idea con That sounds good. No es necesario usar todas las formas en una sola conversación.
rules.pattern: I prefer… / I would rather…
examples: I prefer walking to running.
I would rather stay at home tonight.
Why do we not try a different activity?
rules.tip: Después de would rather no uses to en este patrón: I’d rather go.

questions.prompt: He hopes ___ the club next month.
questions.why: Hope to join es el patrón.

questions.prompt: I would rather ___ at home tonight.

units.story: Our school has started several new clubs. Eva enjoys taking photos and wants to join the photography group. Her friend Ben is interested in learning to cook, but the cooking club meets on the same afternoon as football practice. He does not want to stop playing football, so he decides to attend a weekend cooking class instead. Eva asks Ben to join her on a short photo walk on Saturday. He agrees because he likes spending time outside. They plan to take pictures of interesting buildings and then choose their five favourite photos. Neither of them needs an expensive camera; they will use their phones.

reading.prompt: ¿Por qué Ben busca otra clase de cocina?
reading.why: La clase coincide con football practice.
They will use their phones.

dialogue: What do you enjoy doing in your free time?
I enjoy taking photos and walking.
Would you like to join our photo walk?
Yes, I would. Where are we going?
To the old town. How about meeting at ten?
That sounds good. I will bring my phone.
units.writing: Escribe 60–80 palabras sobre tus aficiones y una actividad nueva. Usa enjoy + -ing, want to, interested in y una razón.
units.model: I enjoy drawing and listening to music in my free time. I am also interested in learning to take better photos. I want to join a photography club because I would like to meet people with the same interests. My friend suggested trying a class on Saturday. I decided to go with her, and we hope to practise in the park afterwards.

listening.text: Our new art club meets on Wednesdays at four. You can try drawing, painting and simple photography. Please bring a notebook, but you do not need to buy paints. This week, we are taking photos outside, so wear comfortable shoes. If you prefer working indoors, another teacher will lead a drawing activity.

units.mission: Elijan una actividad para el fin de semana: cada persona propone dos, explica sus gustos y acuerda una opción común.

units.title: Condiciones y posibilidades
units.goal: Relacionar condiciones con resultados y preparar alternativas.

rules.title: Condiciones posibles
rules.text: El primer condicional combina if + present simple con will + verbo base para un resultado futuro posible. La cláusula con if puede ir primero o después. Cuando va primero, se escribe normalmente una coma entre las partes. No pongas will en la condición básica que practicamos aquí.
rules.pattern: If + presente, will + verbo
examples: If it rains, we will stay indoors.
We will leave early if the weather is good.
If you miss the bus, I will collect you.
rules.tip: En este patrón: If it rains, no If it will rain.

rules.title: Hechos habituales y when
rules.text: Para consecuencias generales o repetidas puede usarse presente en ambas partes: If I go to bed late, I feel tired. When introduce el momento de algo que esperas que ocurra; if presenta una condición. En referencias futuras con when usa presente: I will call when I arrive.
rules.pattern: If + presente, presente / when + presente
examples: If I stay up late, I feel tired.
I will send a message when I arrive.
When the lesson ends, we will have lunch.
rules.tip: Aunque en español uses llegue, en inglés aquí va arrive.

rules.title: May, might y alternativas
rules.text: May y might + verbo base expresan posibilidad, sin asegurar que algo sucederá. Para organizar una salida combina un plan principal con una alternativa: It might rain, so let’s take umbrellas. Unless equivale a if not en casos sencillos; es una ampliación útil, no necesaria para todas tus respuestas.
rules.pattern: It might… / We may…
examples: It might rain this afternoon.
We may change the date.
We will go unless it rains.
rules.tip: No añadas to después de may o might.

questions.prompt: If it ___, we will stay at home.
If you call me, I ___ help you.
I will phone you when I ___.
questions.why: When con referencia futura lleva presente.

questions.prompt: If I sleep badly, I usually ___ tired.
We will go unless it rains. Equivale a…
questions.answer: We will go if it does not rain.
options: We will go if it does not rain.
We will go only if it rains.
We never go when it is dry.
questions.why: Unless significa if not en este caso.

units.story: Our class is planning an outdoor sports day for Friday. If the weather is dry, we will meet on the school field at nine. Everyone should bring water and comfortable shoes. The forecast says it might rain in the afternoon, so we will finish the outdoor games before lunch. If it rains in the morning, we will use the sports hall instead. The teacher will send a message when she decides which place to use. We do not want anyone to travel to the wrong entrance. There may be fewer activities indoors, but everyone will still have a chance to play and work in a team.

reading.prompt: ¿Qué harán si llueve por la mañana?
reading.why: Use the sports hall instead.

reading.answer: Con un mensaje de la profesora.
options: Con un mensaje de la profesora.
Por una carta el mes siguiente.
reading.why: The teacher will send a message.

dialogue: What will we do if it rains on Friday?
We will use the sports hall.
Should I still bring my sports shoes?
Yes, and bring a bottle of water.
When will you confirm the plan?
I will send a message when I check the forecast.
units.writing: Organiza una salida en 60–80 palabras: plan principal, condición, alternativa y cómo avisarás. Incluye if, will, might y when.
units.model: We are planning a picnic on Sunday. If the weather is sunny, we will meet in the park at twelve. It might rain, so we also have another plan. If the ground is wet, we will eat at my house instead. I will send everyone a message when I check the forecast on Saturday evening. Please bring something to drink.

listening.text: Tomorrow will be dry in the morning, but it may rain after two. The temperature will be around eighteen degrees. If you are going to the outdoor market, go early and take a light jacket. The evening may be windy, especially near the river. Sunday should be warmer.

options: Antes de las siete de la mañana.

units.mission: Organiza dos planes para una salida: uno con buen tiempo y otro con lluvia. Explica cuándo confirmarás y qué podría cambiar.

units.title: Dinero y servicios
units.goal: Pedir información, explicar para qué necesitas algo y resolver gestiones sencillas.

rules.title: Expresar finalidad
rules.text: To + verbo explica para qué haces algo: I went to the bank to get some cash. For + nombre explica un uso: a bag for my books. For + -ing puede describir la función de un objeto: a tool for cutting paper. Evita traducir cada para con la misma forma.
rules.pattern: to do / for + nombre
examples: I went to the post office to send a parcel.
I am saving money to buy a bicycle.
This is a bag for my sports clothes.
rules.tip: Para expresar tu objetivo usa to buy, no for buy.

rules.title: Preguntas corteses de información
rules.text: Could you tell me…? introduce una pregunta indirecta. Después, usa orden de afirmación: where the bank is, no where is the bank. Para una pregunta de sí/no usa if: Do you know if it is open? Aprende estos patrones como frases útiles de atención al público.
rules.pattern: Could you tell me where… is?
examples: Could you tell me where the cash machine is?
Do you know if the office is open?
Could you tell me how much it costs?
rules.tip: No mantengas do/does ni inversión en la parte indirecta: how much it costs.

rules.title: Costes y aclaraciones
rules.text: Cost describe el precio; pay for indica qué compras y spend…on en qué gastas dinero o tiempo. How much…? pregunta coste y How long…? duración. En un servicio confirma el total, el plazo y qué formulario necesitas. Si no sabes una palabra, descríbela o pide un ejemplo.
rules.pattern: pay for / spend on / How much does it cost?
examples: How much does it cost to send this parcel?
I spent ten pounds on a notebook.
Do I need to sign this form?
rules.tip: Estas situaciones practican idioma, no recomiendan productos financieros.

questions.prompt: I went to the shop ___ some milk.
This is a box ___ old photos.

questions.why: Orden de afirmación en la pregunta indirecta.
Después de if se usa orden afirmativo.

questions.prompt: I spent five pounds ___ a notebook.
¿Qué pregunta busca el precio del envío?
questions.answer: How much does it cost to send this?
options: How much does it cost to send this?

units.story: Yesterday, Leila went to the post office to send a parcel to her cousin. She had packed a book and a birthday card in a small box.
